reigns.note: Son of Agenor who settled the southern coast of Asia Minor and gave his name to Cilicia — regional Agenorid strand for the coast east of Pamphylia, not a king of Side. No civic residence at Pamphylian Side; city sky stays empty.

Zeus-born son of Europa who carved a kingdom in Lycia; Pausanias cites Pamphylian kinship with Cretans who fled of old with Sarpedon — ethnogenesis of Pamphylia, not a Side king-list. Residences stay Lycia and Troy.

Pausanias says the Pamphylians belong to the Greek race as among those who after Troy wandered with Calchas — post-war settlement wave for the region, not a dwelling at Side. Side itself is named only for the cold Melas that flows past it (8.28.3). Apollodorus Epitome 3.33 lists a Side Achilles took beside Adramyttium — a Mysian coastal town in the Troad raid catalogue, not this Pamphylian city.
